column12: JUDGEMENT on the comparator and the Part. Evkeeza is the closest marketed product: same target (ANGPTL3), same label population (HoFH, adjunct to other LDL-C lowering therapy; book labels table, DailyMed setid 73412138-6d8f-4ea6-bb72-a740190470ff, the October 2025 label reads ages 1 and over). Part B is taken because Evkeeza is a clinician-given IV infusion and Part B holds most of its Medicare use: 63 beneficiaries and $21.8mm against Part D's 27 and $10.8mm in 2024. Case for higher: Part D reads $400,140 per beneficiary; and a Part B beneficiary averaged 8.6 claims (541 / 63) against 13 four-weekly infusions a year, so at $40,378 a claim a full treated year is about $525,000 gross. Case for lower, and it is material: Arrowhead prices below rare-disease comparators. It launched Redemplo in FCS at a $60,000 WAC (per search) against Tryngolza's $595,000 (per search), then cut it to $45,000 a patient-year (8-K 0000879407-26-000045, 2026-05-07). That 'One-REDEMPLO' price was set for a later large sHTG indication; zodasiran has no Phase 3 outside HoFH, so the logic need not carry, but a price well under Evkeeza's is plausible. The uptake calibration below uses this same net price, so the engine reproduces Evkeeza's revenue whatever its true per-patient price

column12: JUDGEMENT: the only US real-world persistence figure for the incumbent in this disease, and the same value is used in the Evkeeza calibration below, so price, stock and starts reconcile. Case for lower: the ELIPSE HoFH open-label extension (Gaudet D et al., Eur Heart J 2024;45(27):2422-2434, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehae325, PMID 38856678) recorded 2 deaths and 3 stops for adverse events among 116 patients over a median 104.3 weeks of exposure, roughly 2.2% a year (other withdrawals not reported in the text); quarterly dosing may also retain better than monthly infusions. Case for higher: one event in 24 patients is a thin base, academic centres retain well, no deaths were recorded, and HoFH carries early cardiovascular death (HICC registry: first major event at a median 37 years in high-income countries, Tromp TR et al., Lancet 2022, PMID 35101175)

Applied to the 340,110,988 US residents of 1 July 2024 (Census Vintage 2024, the figure the zilovertamab, velzatinib and ianalumab seeds carry): 340,110,988 / 300,000 = 1,134
column12: Not carried by the book: lookup.py pool returns nothing for Homozygous, Familial or HoFH, and epidemiology.csv has no row. The book's 'Hypercholesterolemia' pool (23.8mm adults with clinical ASCVD, AZD0780 and enlicitide seeds) is a different indication row and is not narrowed here: HoFH is congenital and counted from birth, many patients are children without ASCVD, and that pool's inflow is heart attacks and strokes. JUDGEMENT to read a Dutch molecular prevalence onto the US. Consistent with Italy's Campania, at least 1 in 320,000 (Di Taranto MD et al., J Clin Med 2020, doi:10.3390/jcm9010219, PMID 31947532). Case for higher: Evkeeza's 2026 US sales run rate equals 652 patients at this seed's net price, 67% of the 12-and-over pool below, which implies either a larger diagnosed population or a higher true price per patient; founder populations push some regions higher. Case for lower: only 50% of Sjouke's molecular cases met the clinical HoFH criteria, and the diagnosed, treatable pool is smaller than the genetic one
